transcript:
Meeting Header: 2027-03-10 14:30 PDT | Duration: 52m | Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Mateo Ruiz (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Mercury - Infra), Tom Beck (Mercury - ML), Ravi Shah (Mercury - Product), Lena Ortiz (Mercury - Security)

Summary: High-level integration discovery focused on SDK support (Python/Node), LangChain and LlamaIndex adapters, gateway/proxy placement, rate limiting/quotas, and observability/tracing hooks. Customer is evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC) with emphasis on latency and compliance.

Topics: SDKs, LangChain, LlamaIndex, gateway/proxy patterns, rate limits/quotas, observability hooks (tracing/events/metrics), security (KMS/SSO/SOC2).

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we wanted to run through how you'd integrate Redwood into your stack, share our SDKs and patterns and hear about your constraints.
[00:18] Aisha: yeah thanks Jordan, quick context - Mercury has a payment orchestration product, we do 200ms median API calls today, latency is pretty sensitive for checkout flows. we're exploring LLM for chat and up-sell scoring, maybe embeddings for product search.
[00:35] Tom: our infra is k8s on AWS, we have a mix of EKS pods and an API gateway in front of things. we use LangChain in our prototype and LlamaIndex for doc store.
[00:50] Priya: great, that aligns. a couple quick Qs on your side - are you leaning hosted/dedicated/private or still open?
[00:58] Ravi: open, but security team will push for VPC/private for production of course. for POC hosted is fine as long as we can do some benching.
[01:12] Jordan: totally. for POC we recommend Hosted API for speed then Dedicated or Private for production depending on isolation and compliance. we can show how the same SDK and routes map across modes.
[01:28] Lena: on compliance - SOC2 yes, we also need KMS integration, audit logs, SSO (SAML). can you send your security docs?
[01:36] Jordan: yes we'll send SOC2 and the security pack after.
[01:42] Mateo: on the integration side, we have language SDKs (Python/Node), REST+gRPC and open telemetry hooks - many customers use our Python SDK inside LangChain chains or as a fired node in LlamaIndex flow.
[01:58] Tom: are there official LangChain and LlamaIndex adapters? we hacked something together but want supported integration.
[02:06] Priya: yes, we maintain example adapters and a repo for LangChain/LLM chains and a LlamaIndex connector. we'll share the repo. caveat: some of the names in the examples show older product naming, sorry for any typos in the repo readme.
[02:22] Aisha: great, about deployment topology, we have an API gateway in front of our services — should Redwood sit behind our gateway or do you recommend proxying at the edge?
[02:33] Mateo: two patterns we see: 1) direct SDK calls from backend services to Redwood endpoint, letting your gateway handle auth and rate limits; or 2) route requests through a customer-managed proxy/gateway for additional VPC peering and logging. For Dedicated/Private we often recommend the proxy pattern to pin traffic through your VPC.
[02:56] Ravi: if we proxy, what's the added latency typically?
[03:02] Priya: depends a lot on network hops; typical extra is 10-30ms when within same region, but if you add extra TLS termination it can be a bit more. we can run a small bench to measure.
[03:18] Tom: about rate limits and quotas - our current traffic shape is spiky around midnight batch jobs, and interactive peaks during business hours. how do you handle per-route quotas and burst tokens?
[03:32] Jordan: we support per-account and per-route limits, with burst windows and throttling policies. default hosted quotas are configurable — most customers start with a baseline and we adjust. for Dedicated you set capacity and autoscaling policies.
[03:47] Priya: also we expose headers and error codes for rate limit backoff so your services can implement retry/backoff.
[03:55] Lena: do you have token-level cost visibility and tracing to tie requests back to routes and users?
[04:02] Mateo: yes, Console gives token breakdown by route, model, and token type; we also offer tracing and spans integration via OpenTelemetry so you can see latency per call. for security we can forward only metadata to your observability backend if you prefer not to send payloads.
[04:20] Aisha: we use Datadog and Splunk - do you integrate?
[04:25] Priya: we have direct exports to Datadog and an option to stream logs to S3 or your SIEM; Splunk customers usually pull from S3 or use our webhooks.
[04:36] Tom: ok on the SDK - latency: does the SDK do streaming responses and chunked generation?
[04:42] Mateo: yes, streaming is supported in SDKs and over websockets/HTTP chunking. for low-latency generation we recommend small prompt sizes and prefix caching for repeated contexts.
[04:55] Ravi: cache - you mentioned KV cache earlier - how does that map to our system?
[05:01] Priya: our runtime maintains KV cache for model context to avoid recomputing previous tokens; we also offer a client-side prefix cache pattern where you cache embedding results or fixed prompts. for embeddings we recommend a caching layer if you have repeated queries.
[05:16] Tom: on LangChain/LlamaIndex, how do you handle function/tool calling and structured outputs?
[05:23] Mateo: function calling and structured output is supported; the SDK returns structured events and the adapters map those into LangChain's tool output or LlamaIndex nodes. sometimes transcription in our examples shows model names slightly off, but functionality is there.
[05:40] Aisha: security question - if we go Dedicated in our VPC, can we use our own KMS/HSM for key management?
[05:48] Jordan: for Private deployments yes; for Dedicated we support customer-managed keys via KMS in some configs. we'll confirm exact architecture in the security doc.
[05:59] Lena: audit logs - need immutable logs with user ids, request metadata, and model/version. can you support that?
[06:06] Mateo: yes we emit audit logs, retention is configurable. we can forward logs to your S3 bucket or push to a SIEM.
[06:14] Tom: about benching - we want to run a throughput test with our typical payloads. how do you recommend doing that without breaking quotas?
[06:22] Priya: we can provision a POC sandbox with increased quotas for the bench run. typically we ask for your sample payloads and expected RPS, run tests against a comparable model variant, and share latency/cost breakdown.
[06:36] Ravi: pricing - we'd like hosted pricing for POC and an estimate on Dedicated monthly commits.
[06:42] Jordan: I'll share the pricing sheet and example commit tiers. for Dedicated, commit size maps to GPU capacity and sustained throughput.
[06:51] Tom: one more on network - if we do proxy inside our VPC to Redwood private endpoint, is there an always-on connection or a peering?
[06:59] Mateo: we support VPC peering and private link options depending on cloud provider. Private/on-prem can be air-gapped if needed.
[07:10] Aisha: any gotchas integrating with LlamaIndex? we saw some tokenization mismatch experiments.
[07:17] Priya: tokenization can differ between models; we recommend normalizing tokens during pre-processing and using our tokenizer libs in SDK. LlamaIndex connectors usually need a small shim to handle chunking and embeddings.
[07:31] Ravi: on the topic of competitors - we evaluated Anthropic and some cloud endpoints; what differentiates Redwood for us?
[07:39] Jordan: our focus is production-first: same API across hosted/dedicated/private, strong observability, and cost controls like batching and quantization suggestions. we also help with rollout policies - canary, A/B and automatic fallback to cheaper variants.
[07:56] Lena: can you provide examples of policy config? like automatic fallback if latency > X?
[08:03] Priya: yes, the Console exposes rollout policies with threshold triggers; we can share an example JSON for your ops team.
[08:12] Tom: integration complexity - how long to get a minimal POC running?
[08:16] Jordan: typically 1-2 weeks: quickstart with Hosted, LangChain adapter, basic quotas. Dedicated on-boarding is longer (a few weeks) due to infra and networking. Private is the longest due to compliance.
[08:30] Aisha: ok good. for the POC we'll start with Hosted and LangChain integration, if bench passes we'll evaluate Dedicated.
[08:38] Ravi: about observability hooks - can we get request-level traces with model prompts redacted?
[08:44] Mateo: yes, you can enable metadata-only tracing; payloads can be redacted or omitted based on config.
[08:52] Tom: any SDK quirks across languages? our stack is mostly Python but a few Node microservices.
[08:59] Priya: parity across SDKs is pretty good; Node streaming semantics differ slightly but examples are provided. for LangChain we have Python-first examples, Node adapters are community-supported but we can help.
[09:12] Aisha: questions from Security - is there a documented data flow diagram for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private?
[09:19] Jordan: yes we'll attach a data flow diagram in the security pack.
[09:24] Lena: encryption at rest and in transit?
[09:27] Mateo: all traffic is TLS; at rest we use AES-256, and for customer-managed keys we integrate with KMS/HSM options.
[09:36] Ravi: can we get a sample API key rotation flow?
[09:40] Priya: yes we support key rotation with audit trails, and RBAC for key management in Console.
[09:48] Tom: on quotas again - do you support per-API-key quotas and per-route quotas? we have internal teams that must be rate-limited differently.
[09:56] Jordan: yes, per-key and per-route quotas are supported, and you can define policies in Console or via API.
[10:03] Aisha: any recommended defaults for retries/backoff?
[10:07] Mateo: typically exponential backoff with jitter, respecting 429 headers; we include recommended client-side middleware in SDKs.
[10:15] Ravi: ok, let's talk about observability details - what metrics do you expose out of the box?
[10:20] Priya: latency percentiles, token counts, cost per call, model version, route, http status, and custom tags. export via OTLP to your backend.
[10:32] Tom: do you emit model internal metrics like decode time vs forward time?
[10:37] Mateo: we surface helpful breakdowns (kernel time, queuing, decode) in per-model dashboards for enterprise customers.
[10:45] Aisha: any limits on streaming websockets connections?
[10:49] Priya: we have connection limits per account but can increase for Dedicated. we'll share defaults.
[10:56] Lena: compliance follow up - can you support data residency in EU?
[11:01] Jordan: yes we have EU regions and can constrain data residency for enterprise customers.
[11:07] Ravi: next step for bench - we'll share 24 hours of representative traffic and some sample payloads.
[11:12] Priya: perfect, we'll provision a sandbox and propose a bench plan.
[11:18] Jordan: recap - we'll send pricing, security pack, LangChain/LlamaIndex examples and schedule deep technical bench next week.
[11:27] Tom: sounds good.
[11:30] Aisha: thanks all.

Action Items (recap): Jordan to send pricing and security docs; Priya to share LangChain/LlamaIndex repo; Tom to provide sample payloads and metrics; schedule deep-dive and bench.

End of meeting.
